newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed higher in lifeless trading with most gains registered at the opening as traders looked forlornly ahead to next week for some action.
Dealers seized on a change in composition of the J.P. Morgan Dutch bond index next week as a factor which enliven trading, saying it could spark more extension trades.
The guilder yield curve steepened somewhat between two and five years, with Dutch bonds outperforming German equivalents.
A dealer said he had heard of a large professional buyer of January 2004 paper in an otherwise dull market. "Looking at the futures, they have done nothing," he said.
He said institutions had decided to sit on their cash holdings because they felt prices were still too high.
A London-based dealer said fund managers had in recent times been overwhelmed with presentations by securities houses on the prospects for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
He said all of the various scenarios presented seemed plausible. "They haven't got a clue what to do next because they're completely confused," he said.
Looking ahead, the dealer said the duration of the J.P. Morgan index for Dutch bonds would increase next week when the 6.25 percent July 1998 state loan dropped out of the index.
The London dealer said fund managers measured against the index would be forced to buying longer guilder paper to keep matching the index for duration.
Some had already completed their transactions but others were still to act. "It will keep guilders relatively buoyant," he added.
A trader said he had seen buying of the 5.75 percent 2007 10-year benchmark Dutch state loan and longer bonds in tandem with selling of the July 1998s.
But he said the July 1998s would find buying support from money market funds.
